done.why: I had read enough to judge the writing and stopped early after a short wander through the barrow, cavern and garden.

about: A Zork II-style underground world with a lantern and sword, a Wizard who appears when you light the lamp, a ravine, and a formal garden. Treasures lie south of the ravine, and the Wizard's spells make things that are not really there.

moments.note: Lighting the lamp summons the Wizard, who glances at my empty hands and tells me where the treasure is.
The gold ingot the Wizard conjured can't be taken, and the refusal is written with wry grace.
A basilisk is listed in the room but examining it says I can't see it.
The newspaper has been rewritten to hint at the whirring room and the Wizard's loot.

wished: To be able to examine the basilisk.
To see more of the world, including the stone door and the whirring room.

lines.line: It has that look of a thing that has been through one adventure already and would rather not discuss it.
lines.why: Dry, characterful description of the lantern.

lines.line: the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: A funny, inventive way to refuse taking an illusion.

engagement.why: The Wizard's hints gave me a goal and made me want to go on.

difficulty.why: Early play was easy, with clear directions given.

interestingness.why: Familiar Zork material was reworked with illusions and new hints.

prose.why: Witty, precise and confident prose, especially in the new lines layered over the classic text.
